response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) >= '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) <= '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender) SELECT gender, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM g) AS above_average_by FROM g WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM g) ORDER BY order_count DESC

assumptions.assumption: The period is inclusive of both endpoints, with date_order_placed compared as text.
The average is taken across the gender groups (the mean of per-gender order counts), not across individual orders or customers.
Customers with a NULL gender form their own group, which counts toward the average and could be shown. An inner join to Customers excludes orders with no matching customer.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude customers with NULL gender, so the average is taken only over non-null genders.
alternatives.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) >= '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) <= '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender) SELECT gender, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM g) AS above_average_by FROM g WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM g) ORDER BY order_count DESC
